Params: Under dazzling sunlight, several athletic figures race across the track, drawing waves of applause and cheers.
As for the figure standing in the shade of the trees... They could slip away at any moment, and no one would ever think to look for them.
<phonetic=The Nameless Dreamer>He</phonetic> is someone who has always stood in the shadows.

Even when he tries to run, he can never swing his arms with the same ease as the other athletes. It doesn't matter how hard he pushes—he'll always end up tripping, sprawled in the sand beside the track.
There you are! Didn't you sign up for the 1500-meter? It's about to start, you know. Come on, let's go!
S-Sorry, but I'm not feeling well today.
That's a lie. The truth is, everyone on the track looks too dazzling for him. He knows that there's no way he could ever keep up with them.
If anything, he wouldn't be here if it weren't for his class egging him on. That's what tricked him into believing that maybe, just maybe, he could pull something off if he tried.
In that case, he might as well quit before he can even lose. Perhaps that way, he'd look less pathetic.
Oh... I see. Go get some rest then.
His classmate doesn't press further, simply offering a caring smile before walking away.
But <phonetic=The Nameless Dreamer>he</phonetic> hears it clearly. He hears that muttered remark as the classmate turns away, one spoken just loud enough to reach his ears.
Shouldn't have signed up if it's gonna be like this. Attention craving bastard.
I sincerely apologize. The fault lies with me...
I must admit, I expected so much more from you. We wouldn't have hired you otherwise.

I hope you do realize that your efficiency compared to your coworker is... night and day, to say the least. Now then, go think about where exactly you fall short, and why this project should be yours to handle.
I hope that next time, you'll be able to demonstrate some critical thinking, and not just a simple progress report.

He's been lectured this same way more times than he can count. If he just keeps his head down, the storm will naturally pass, just as always. Just five minutes... and everything will go back to normal.
But for some reason, today, he chose to raise his head.
But... everyone in the company said this project couldn't be done. We were the only ones to even give it a try.
The expected tirade never comes. The middle-aged man, usually so quick to speak his mind, simply flicks his lighter and ignites a cigarette in silence.
You don't actually think telling me you tried your best means anything, do you?
Please. How many years have you been working now? Grow up already.
His gaze might have held only disappointment before, but now, there's unmistakably a trace of scorn in his eyes.
This is a company, not your home.
The only person in this world who'll forgive your mistakes unconditionally is your mother.
Why can't you understand? The only person I have left to count on now... is you!
The gaunt woman suddenly seizes his shoulders, clutching him like one final piece of driftwood in a raging sea, shaking him desperately.
Why does nothing ever go our way...? Your father got fired, and now our family is drowning in debt...
Why can't you just do better?! Why can't you give your mother some peace of mind for once?!
He's heard these same words countless times since childhood, but no matter how many times she's questioned him, he's never been able to give her the perfect answer she expects.
And so <phonetic=The  Nameless  Dreamer>    he    </phonetic> buries all his emotions within a single numb nod.
...I'll do better, Mom. I'll figure something out. Don't worry.
Everything piles up little by little, eventually becoming the final piece that brings the precarious tower crashing down.
He's painstakingly held this life together until now, never daring to let his guard down for even a moment. But a single lapse of control was all it took for it to all shatter.
Which incident was it that finally set him off? <phonetic=The Nameless Dreamer>He</phonetic> can no longer say for certain.
Though, when he finally threw that punch with every ounce of hatred crystallized within it...
In that instant, <phonetic=The Nameless Dreamer>he</phonetic> did in fact feel a fleeting sense of release.
He snaps back to reality. At some point, he's walked all the way to a rooftop. The night wind blows around him.
He gazes at the glowing city. It's shimmering as brilliantly as ever. Just then, a vast and nameless emptiness wells up inside him.
If I just... jumped, would all of this just go away?
Who am I kidding... even if someone like me jumped, the world wouldn't be affected in the slightest.
He lets out a bitter laugh. Just as he's about to step back from the edge, a sweet voice cuts through the cold wind.
Then... would you like to come to my world instead?
Her voice is clear and pure.
I do not know how you see yourself, or how you see this world.
But to me, "you" are very important.
He turns to see a slender, willowy figure, her dress billowing like sails in the wind as she floats in the sky.
Wouldn't you like to have a chance to turn it all around?
If there is a world where anything you wish for comes true... Just what punishment awaits them... and what would your future be like?
How about it? Would you like to see it for yourself?

He wavers. In that moment, the one thing <phonetic=The Nameless Dreamer>he</phonetic> is thinking would undoubtedly be this—even if it's just once, if he really does get a chance to do whatever he wishes without consequences, that'd be wonderful.
So <phonetic=The  Nameless  Dreamer>    he    </phonetic> takes a step forward without hesitation.
Even though he knows full well that only the abyss awaits.
I'll go with you. I want to use what little I have left however I please.
<color=#ff4e4eff><size=60><o=000000ff|0.5>"Hahaha! Of course! Everything will be exactly as you wish!!!"</o></size></color>
"Hahaha! Of course! Everything will be exactly as you wish!!!"
And then, everything dissolves into warm, lingering embers.
He's torn between bliss and agony. He's gained everything he ever wanted, only to lose the ability to feel any joy from it.
Whenever he tries to escape, the sweet dream weaves itself into a soft, smothering cocoon that wraps around him once more.
It doesn't matter whether he fights to stay conscious or surrender to the abyss. Either way, his soul will be torn apart by the unbearable pain.
So he chooses to stop thinking altogether and steps through the "door" once more.
"If I give up the soul that can feel pain as well, then surely this time I'll find true release." So he thinks.
<phonetic=The  Nameless  Dreamer>    He    </phonetic> hangs suspended by countless threads within the Deep Dream, trapped at the center of the Nightmares.
Once you become a Nightmare, there's no going back. I've ruined everything again.
It's not that he doesn't know what he's done, or that he doesn't see how grotesque he's become.
If you go back through the "door" now, you won't be tainted by the Nightmares...
I know I screwed up. But... I'm really not in the mood to hear some meaningless lecture right now.
Honestly, I'm not arrogant enough to lecture you either.

People who think they can gain a complete understanding of someone's life and pass judgment with just a few words, before casually throwing around talk of redemption... In my eyes, that is what's truly revolting.
The girl in the red dress stands before the "nest" woven from threads, raising her flintlock at the young man and the Nightmares thrashing wildly behind him.
If this truly is a choice you made after careful thought, then I won't say anything.
However, if you ask me, I only see a man who's chosen to run away again in the face of despair.
Since you've given up on your own life... I'll put an end to your cowardice myself.
What if I told you there's still a chance to turn this around?
You step forward and lower the gun in the girl's hand.
You mentioned that time flows differently in the Dream City.
In that case, can you send him a few days into the past like you did back then?
I could, but I'm sure you also understand that he won't change his mind, even if I did so, yes?
Once this chaotic dream world shatters and we return to reality, time will flow normally again. Everything that happened will still occur as it did.
The girl's tone is anything but categorical. She simply states the facts calmly.
You remember our agreement with the Dream Master, yes?
We get rid of the Nightmares for her, and in return, she helps us find a way out of here.
Even if I send his consciousness back, as long as he chooses to give up on himself again, we'll still have to put an end to this with our own hands.
Even so, I believe everyone deserves a second chance.
He came here to start over, didn't he? It shouldn't end like this.
The girl says nothing and simply takes a step back in silence.
You step forward, reach out, and begin tearing away the threads coiled around the dreamer's body, strand by strand.
The corruption of the Nightmares recedes, and the filthy mud beneath his feet dissolves. Human limbs gradually emerge from the crimson.
See? Changing yourself isn't as hard as you think.
That's not something for me to decide. It's a trial that you must face once you return.
The last thread peels away from the young man's body. He plummets, crashing down on one knee into the dark mire below him.
Personally, though, if you no longer fear even death itself...
Then I'm pretty sure nothing in this world will be able to faze you.
Brilliant golden light ignites in the girl's left eye. The power of the Angel, harbinger of time's reversal, stirs to life.
Will you give up on your life just like that, or struggle desperately one more time...
Before we go back... There are two things I need to tell you.
The young man struggles to stand up in the mire, then slowly walks toward the barrel of the girl's gun.
The one who invited me and trapped me in this place, as well as your true enemy, is called "The Oneiros."
He reaches out and presses down on the grip, trembling.
His hands, caked in black mud, pull the trigger. The bullet loaded in Zafkiel pierces straight into his heart.
With that, the young man called Seki begins to fade away like a reflection on water scattered by the wind—
Until he completely and quietly vanished. From before the barrel of her gun, as well as this nightmarish mire.
Without despair to sustain it, the Deep Dream rapidly folds in on itself, contracting and expelling the two intruders from this small domain.
The girl lifts the hem of her dress, takes the human by the hand, and aims the barrel skyward.
The bullet soars toward the heavens, tearing through the darkness, pulling every thread back to the point of origin.
When you open your eyes again, you're already back in the bustling plaza.
The warm afternoon sun, white pigeons wandering across the cobblestones, tourists laughing and chatting away... Everything is as it should be.
Except for one thing, that is—the dejected young man who was on the bench, the one named Seki, is nowhere to be found.
Yet at the same time, nothing seems to have changed at all.
Sorry for the bother. Would you mind if I asked you something?

Before you can even process what's happening, the girl beside you has already started walking over to a group of high school girls chatting by the street. She's waving cheerfully, acting like they're old friends.
(Whatever, she's better suited for this than I am anyway.)
Female Student by the Road A
Surprisingly, not only do they not seem bothered, but they actually move closer to her.
Female Student by the Road B
By the way, what's with the outfit of this person here?
Female Student by the Road A
Ooh, you've even got a knife on you! What company do you work for? This all-black look is totally awesome!
(Not that they'd understand even if I tried to explain.)
It's nothing much. I'd just like to ask you about some rumors that have been going around.
I heard some creature called "Nightmare" has been lurking in the back alleys around this area. Apparently, they would drag people away and eat them. I must admit, this has given me quite the fright.
Kurumi strikes up a conversation with them, her tone so friendly it's almost like she's become a different person.
Have you happened to hear anything about this?
The two female students, crepes in hand, pause for a moment. They exchange glances for a few seconds and break into a chuckle.
Come on, what kinda joke is that?
There's never been anything like that around here. It's always been super peaceful!
